questions.text: Tell me about a time your inventory analysis led to a direct improvement in service levels.

key_points: Analysis performed: fill rate, days-on-hand, stockout frequency
Insight surfaced: which SKUs were under-stocked and why
Replenishment change and service level improvement

questions.text: Describe a time you built or improved an inventory reporting dashboard.

key_points: What decisions it needed to support
Metrics chosen and data source integration
Adoption by planning and commercial teams

questions.text: Tell me about a time you identified root cause of a recurring inventory discrepancy.

key_points: Investigation: cycle count, shrinkage, system vs physical
Root cause: process gap, scanning error, theft, system config
Fix implemented and recurrence rate reduction

questions.text: Describe a time you supported a strategic inventory reduction programme.

key_points: Data: identified excess by coverage, demand probability, lifecycle
Scenario modelling: reduction impact on service level
Programme results: working capital freed without service damage
avoid: Cut across the board without segmentation

questions.text: Tell me about a time you developed or improved a demand segmentation model.

key_points: Previous segmentation shortcoming: too simple or not updated
New model: ABC-XYZ or clustering approach
Planning policy differentiation by segment and outcome

questions.text: How do you calculate days of inventory on hand (DOH) and what does it tell you?

key_points: Formula: (average inventory / COGS) × days in period
Interpretation: coverage weeks at current demand rate
Context: benchmark vs target by SKU category
strong_answer_signals: Forward-looking: based on forecast not just historical

questions.text: What analysis would you run to identify your top excess inventory priorities?

key_points: Coverage in weeks vs target by SKU
Value at risk: quantity × unit cost × probability of obsolescence
Age of stock: FIFO compliance, expiry risk
avoid: Volume only with no value weighting

questions.text: How would you use SQL or Python to analyse inventory movement patterns across 10,000 SKUs?

key_points: SQL: window functions for running stock balance, GROUP BY for ABC
Python: pandas for time-series, matplotlib for trend visualisation
Output: segmented report with action flags
strong_answer_signals: Actionable output not just data dump

questions.text: How do you reconcile system inventory to physical inventory after a cycle count?

key_points: Compare system vs physical by location and SKU
Investigate discrepancies above threshold before adjusting
Root cause by type: process, shrinkage, scan error
avoid: No threshold — investigate everything or nothing

questions.text: How would you build a model to predict which SKUs are at risk of becoming obsolete?

key_points: Features: demand trend slope, lifecycle stage, substitution rate, age of stock
Model: logistic regression or simple scoring model
Output: risk score with recommended action by tier

questions.text: A planner is relying on an inventory report you produce that you suspect contains an error. What do you do?

key_points: Validate the suspected error before flagging
Notify the planner immediately with the corrected data
Fix the source and add a validation check to prevent recurrence

questions.text: You are asked to produce a monthly inventory health report in two days instead of the usual five. What do you do?

key_points: Scope negotiation: full report or priority metrics only
Fast path: automate data pulls already built
Communicate any limitations of accelerated report

questions.text: You notice a warehouse is holding 12 months of stock on a slow-moving SKU that is nearing expiry. No one owns the decision to liquidate it. What do you do?

key_points: Quantify the risk: value at risk, expiry date, liquidation options
Escalate with options to the right decision maker
Propose liquidation channel and timeline
strong_answer_signals: Did not wait for ownership to appear
avoid: Tried to decide alone without authority

questions.text: Senior leadership wants a single inventory KPI to track. What do you recommend and why?

key_points: Inventory turns or GMROI as primary KPI balances cost and return
Explain why single KPI must be balanced with service level guardrail
Propose composite or paired metric to prevent optimising in isolation
avoid: Refused to recommend — gave too many metrics

questions.text: A new ERP system is being implemented and your team is asked to validate the opening inventory data migration. How do you approach this?

key_points: Row count and value reconciliation: old vs new system
Sample validation of individual SKU balances by location
Business rules validation: negative stock, zero-cost items, unit of measure
strong_answer_signals: Both aggregate and sample level checks
Business rule testing beyond just quantities

questions.text: What aspects of inventory analysis do you find most intellectually rewarding?

key_points: Specific: forecasting, optimisation, root cause, dashboard design
Why: connection to real operational outcomes
How it connects to this role

questions.text: How have you developed your inventory analysis skills over your career?

key_points: Formal: APICS/CPIM, Excel/BI tools, SQL/Python
Informal: on-the-job projects, mentors, self-study
Most impactful development experience

questions.text: How do you ensure data quality and trust in inventory reporting across your team?

key_points: Automated data quality checks in pipeline
Single source of truth: one agreed data model
Issue escalation protocol and SLA for corrections

questions.text: How would you measure and report on inventory accuracy in a multi-site warehouse operation?

key_points: Location accuracy: system vs physical by SKU-location pair
Cycle count plan: ABC frequency — A=weekly, B=monthly, C=quarterly
Site-level scorecard with trend and root cause summary

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with commercial teams to incorporate market intelligence into inventory plans.

key_points: Commercial insight: promotion, ranging change, competitive action
How you translated it into demand adjustment or safety stock
Inventory and service outcome
avoid: Statistical only with no market intelligence

questions.text: What is GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment) and how do you use it?

key_points: Formula: gross margin / average inventory cost
Use: identifies which products generate most return per dollar of inventory
Action: shift assortment and inventory weight to high GMROI SKUs
strong_answer_signals: Used to inform buying or ranging decisions

questions.text: Your inventory turns target is being missed despite service levels being good. How do you diagnose and fix it?

key_points: Identify which SKUs are dragging turns: coverage analysis
Separate excess driven by over-buying vs demand miss
Corrective actions: parameter change, supplier MOQ negotiation, clearance

questions.text: Describe a time you identified a supplier that was consistently delivering short quantities or incorrect items.

key_points: Detected via goods-in discrepancy data and trend analysis
Quantified financial and service impact
Raised formal supplier performance issue with procurement
avoid: One-off investigation with no pattern analysis
